subject: Demo recap + proposed pilot / evaluation sprint — Lighthouse Health
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed pilot / evaluation sprint — Lighthouse Health

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. I wanted to capture a short recap of the demo and a concrete, timeboxed proposal for a pilot (evaluation sprint) so your team has something to review with procurement and the clinical informatics team. Below is an outline we propose; happy to iterate.

Quick recap from today
- Demo focus: clinical note summarization + coding recommendation prompts, low-latency generation for clinician workflows, and redaction controls for PHI.
- Key asks you mentioned: ~100 concurrent clinicians, sub-300ms median token latency for short summaries, on-prem / VPC deployment for auditability.

Proposed evaluation sprint (3-week, lightweight pilot) — goals and success criteria
1) Week 0 — Kickoff & data prep (3 business days)
   - Deliverables: NDA/SoW kick-off, sample data ingest (anonymized clinical notes), access to a test VPC.
   - Success criteria: Redwood receives 500 sample notes + sample schema, procurement acknowledges SOW timeline.
2) Week 1 — Baseline integration & smoke tests (5 business days)
   - Redwood tasks: deploy evaluation model in a customer-dedicated VPC, connect to SFTP/s3 test bucket, run basic inference.
   - Customer tasks: provide test credentials, feedback on output format.
   - Success criteria: End-to-end pipeline completes for ~200 notes; median response time <500ms for short summaries.
3) Week 2 — Quality tuning & workflows (5 business days)
   - Redwood tasks: run brief prompt sweep, tune temperature/stop sequences, enable PHI redaction rules, provide 3 candidate templates for clinician-facing summaries.
   - Customer tasks: run clinician review with 10-15 sample users, provide qualitative feedback and example failure modes.
   - Success criteria: ≥80% of reviewed summaries rated acceptable by clinicians (basic rubric to be shared).
4) Week 3 — Performance validation & handoff (5 business days)
   - Redwood tasks: run a 1000-note throughput test, provide latency and cost estimate for production, deliver a short technical playbook for next steps.
   - Customer tasks: procurement and security sign-off on pilot artifacts.
   - Success criteria: throughput target met within committed config, and procurement confirms path to Dedicated or Private deployment.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Alex Martinez (AE) — program lead; Priyom Das (Solutions Eng) — technical owner.
- Lighthouse Health: Sara Li — project sponsor; procurement contact included for next steps.

Attachments included: redwood_eval_sprint_outline_v1.pdf (detailed timeline), data_ingest_sample_schema.csv (sample schema we need).

Next steps I recommend
- You review the outline internally with procurement and clinical informatics.
- If that looks reasonable, can we lock in the kickoff for Monday, Aug 23?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync if folks prefer to walk through.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Redwood Inference — inference that scales for production

From: Sara Li <sara.li@lighthousehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lighthouse Health Procurement <procurement@lighthousehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed pilot / evaluation sprint — Lighthouse Health

Alex —

Appreciate the clear recap and proposed plan. High-level notes from our side:
- Procurement will need a short SoW + estimated cost range for the 3-week pilot (ballpark is fine for now).
- Security wants to confirm logging retention and KMS integration before Week 0 — can you include a short security appendix?
- Clinicians want the summary templates to include explicit "actionable findings" and a 30–50 word TL;DR at the top.

We can tentatively target Aug 23 kickoff but procurement wants the SoW in hand by EOD Fri (Aug 20) to approve scheduling.

Also, one constraint: our internal data team can only deliver anonymized extracts via S3 with a specific prefix pattern (we'll share details).

Would you and Priyom be able to draft the SoW + a one-page security appendix and send to procurement by Friday? If so, please cc me and I'll route.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Director, Clinical Informatics
Lighthouse Health
Sara.Li@lighthousehealth.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Demo recap + proposed pilot / evaluation sprint — Lighthouse Health

Folks — forwarding Sara's response. Procurement needs an SoW + security appendix by EOD Fri (Aug 20). Sara called out two technical asks: S3 prefix delivery + KMS/log retention details.

Action items for Priyom:
- Draft a 1-page security appendix: KMS options, logging/retention defaults, SOC2 controls we surface for the pilot.
- Prepare a short technical SoW section listing data ingest steps and required credentials (S3 prefix).
- Quick sanity-check on perf targets: confirm that the proposed config can hit median <500ms for short summaries at these volumes.

Jonas — can you review the SoW/security appendix before I send to the customer? If you're tight this week, a quick greenlight is fine.

Thanks — aiming to have a draft to Sara & procurement by Friday.

—Alex

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo recap + proposed pilot / evaluation sprint — Lighthouse Health

Alex / Jonas —

Thanks — I drafted both artifacts and uploaded them to Drive (link below). High-level summary of what's in the security appendix:
- KMS: support for customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (we'll document required IAM roles).
- Logging: request-level tracing enabled for pilot; default retention 30 days but we can extend for a fee — noted for procurement.
- Data handling: on-disk encryption, in-flight TLS, and an optional data-redaction step we can apply during ingestion.
- SOC2: we included a two-paragraph summary of our SOC2 scope and an audit contact.

Performance sanity check: I ran the proposed model in a dedicated test instance with a 2x burst capacity config. For 100 concurrent short requests the median token latency for summaries was ~320ms (95th ~750ms). I think we can comfortably hit the Week 1 target with the proposed config; I'll call out the exact instance/quantization combo in the SoW.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D/view

If that looks good, Alex — feel free to send to Sara & procurement. Jonas, if you have any edits to the security wording happy to incorporate.

—Priyom
